question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=x$ along the line $y=4 x,$ $\,0\le x\le 4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the given curve is of the form $y=y(x).$ Therefore, by setting $x=t,$ we have $y=y(t)=4 t.$ This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\langle t,4 t\rangle,\qquad 0\le t\le 4
$$

Computing $\mathbf r^{\prime}(t)$ and $\|\mathbf r^{\prime}(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}\mathbf i+\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dt}\mathbf j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}(t)\mathbf i+\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}(4 t)\mathbf j \\ &=\mathbf i+(4)\mathbf j \\ \|\mathbf r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt})^2+(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dt})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{1^2+(4)^2} \\ &=\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm ds&=\int_{0}^{4}f(r(t))\|\mathbf r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm dt \\ &=\int_{0}^{4}(t)(\sqrt{17})\,\mathrm dt \\ &=\left[\frac{\sqrt{17} t^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{4} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}\left((4)^{2}-(0)^{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{2}\left(16-0\right) \\ &=8 \sqrt{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{x-y}$ along the line $y=x-4,$ $\,0\le x\le 7.$

\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-4)j \\  & =i+\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}

$$
